Title: Source 3: The Natchez
Content: This drawing shows a Plaquemine village at the Holly Bluff site in Mississippi. The Plaquemine were ancestors¹ of the Natchez. Like the Plaquemine, the Natchez built mounds in their villages. The mounds were topped with sacred² buildings where they held religious services. The Natchez lived on family farms near the mounds. They grew corn, beans, and squash. They hunted, fished, and gathered wild plants for food.
The Natchez also made tools, such as the animal-bone awls shown in the picture. Awls are used for poking holes in things.
References: sacred: important in a religious way
